topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Distance Analogy
lecture_lines: Derivatives represent the rate of change.
Integrals measure the accumulation of change.
A speedometer shows the current velocity.
Distance is the total area accumulated.
animations: Create a car element at left, color #FFFFFF.
Animate car moving right, creating a rectangular area beneath.
Highlight area represents distance traveled, color #00FF00.

sections.title: Visualizing the Inverse Operation
lecture_lines: Derivatives find the slope of a curve.
Integrals find the area under a curve.
animations: Show graph of velocity, horizontal line at y=v.
Highlight the area under the curve as integral.
Show the inverse movement: retrieving area from curve.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
lecture_lines: The Fundamental Theorem connects these two.
Integrating the rate gives net change.
It equals final position minus initial.
animations: Display a function f(x) curve in #FF00FF.
Define area function A(x) = integral f(t)dt.
Show moving vertical line at x, color #FFFFFF.
Visualize area accumulating as x moves right.
State derivative of A(x) is f(x).

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: The theorem bridges these geometric concepts.
animations: Show the inverse relationship formula clearly.
Concluding animation: showing integration path back to original.
